newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk says asset seizures threatened over taxes.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk says asset seizures threatened over taxes.

text.p: Top officials of Russia's Norilsk Nickel will meet tax officials this week who have threatened to seize assets of the nickel and copper producer over tax arrears, a Norilsk representative said on Wednesday.
Yuri Oleinikov, head of Norilsk's public relations in Moscow, said Federal Tax Service authorities had not seized any metal or property.
"They have not taken anything, just threatened to do so," he said. "But they could freeze property as well as metal."
He denied market talk that tax officials had frozen thousands of tonnes of nickel.

He declined to say precisely what the government had threatened to seize or how much AO Norilsky Nikel 0#NKEL.RUO owed in tax arrears, but said the company had paid taxes regularly over the past two months.
Russia is cracking down on major firms over tax arrears.
Norilsk reported consolidated pre-tax profit for 1995 of nearly five trillion roubles and net profit under Russian accounting rules of 138 billion roubles.
The Kommersant Daily newspaper said the company owed about five trillion roubles to the federal budget.
Norilsk, which has spoken publicly of its financial difficulties, won a small reprieve in August when President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree delaying some of its debt repayments.
It said in September that its total debt, including wage and other arrears, was 13 trillion roubles.

Pyotr Mostovoi, head of the Federal Bankruptcy Agency, said on Wednesday Russia had sent AO Norilskgazprom, a Norilsk-based natural gas enterprise with tax debts of 580 billion roubles, a notice to pay up or face possible bankruptcy proceedings. He said the gas firm was not formally part of the metals group.
